slideshowEditor.renderConfirmBody1: {{photos}} becomes about {{minutes}} of video. Every one is re-encoded frame by frame, which is the heaviest thing this server does.
slideshowEditor.renderConfirmBody2: Expect several minutes, and longer on a small machine. It runs at low priority in the background — you can leave this page — but the rest of the server may feel slower while it works.
slideshowEditor.renderConfirmBody3: Nothing is changed until it finishes, and you can stop it at any time from the control panel’s Tasks page.
slideshowEditor.staleBody: This movie doesn’t include your latest changes. Re-render to update it.
slideshowEditor.renderingHint: Rendering runs in the background and can take a few minutes — you can leave this page and come back. The server is working hard while this runs, so everything else on it may feel slower; you can stop it from the control panel’s Tasks page.
slideshowEditor.exportHintBase: Export a downloadable MP4 of your photos and videos, transitions{{musicClause}}.
slideshowEditor.titleClauseOn: The movie opens with the title card set above — its words, its length, and whether it sits on black, a photo, or a collage.
slideshowEditor.titleClauseOff: There is no title card, so the movie opens straight on the first photo.
slideshowEditor.exportHintTail: Rendering runs in the background and can take a few minutes for a large slideshow. Ken Burns exports as a crossfade, and Random varies the transition at every cut. When a default movie library is set, the finished movie is also saved to your gallery.
slideshowEditor.emptyBody: This slideshow is empty. Use “Add photos” above to browse your galleries by folder, or select photos in the Timeline and use “Add to slideshow”.
slideshowEditor.movieFiledAs: Saved into your gallery as {{name}} — a re-render replaces that copy.
slideshowEditor.movieNotFiled: This movie lives here only. Use “Save to…” to keep a copy in one of your galleries.
slideshowEditor.movieSaveFailedTitle: The movie rendered, but wasn't saved to the library
slideshowEditor.movieWillFileAs: When it's made, it will be saved into your gallery as {{name}}.
